Bibingka (Traditional Filipino Baked Rice Cake)

Served at: Gaudete Sunday

Serves 6-8Prep 20 minCook 30 min

Bibingka is a beloved Filipino rice cake, traditionally enjoyed after attending Simbang Gabi (dawn masses) during the Advent season, which includes Gaudete Sunday. This festive treat symbolizes warmth, community, and the joyful anticipation of Christmas, making it a perfect dish to share during this period of rejoicing.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (240 g) glutinous rice flour
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 tablespoon (15 g) baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) salt
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) coconut milk
  • 2-3 large banana leaves, softened
  • 2 salted duck eggs, sliced
  • 1/2 cup (50 g) grated cheddar cheese
  • 2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter or margarine, melted, for brushing
  • 1/2 cup (50 g) fresh grated coconut, for topping

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). If using traditional bibingka molds, line them with softened banana leaves. If using a baking pan, line it with banana leaves, ensuring they extend slightly over the edges.
  2. To soften banana leaves, carefully pass them over an open flame (like a gas burner) for a few seconds until they become pliable and change to a brighter green color. Be careful not to burn them.
  3. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the glutinous rice flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt until well combined.
  4. In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs and coconut milk together until smooth.
  5. Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, mixing continuously until a smooth, lump-free batter is formed. Do not overmix.
  6. Pour the batter into the prepared banana leaf-lined molds or baking pan, filling them about two-thirds full.
  7. Arrange the slices of salted duck egg and half of the grated cheddar cheese on top of the batter.
  8. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean and the top is golden brown.
  9. Once removed from the oven, immediately brush the tops of the bibingka generously with melted butter or margarine.
  10. Sprinkle the remaining grated cheddar cheese and the fresh grated coconut over the warm bibingka.
  11. Serve warm, directly from the molds or cut into wedges if using a baking pan.

Tips

  • For an authentic smoky flavor, you can use a traditional clay oven (pugon) or a grill with a lid and hot coals on top and bottom.
  • If you don't have salted duck eggs, you can omit them or use regular hard-boiled eggs for a milder flavor.
  • Experiment with other toppings like latik (coconut milk curds) or a drizzle of condensed milk for added sweetness.
